# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Bank Statement Labeling Codebase Report

## Directory structure overview

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn Flask app on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask/pandas/fuzzywuzzy package
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + per-bank pipeline orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific parsers (category + partyName)
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Cross-bank enrichment
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF cleanup + sep_by_* / py_extract helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Subcategory / merchant regex dictionary
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific extraction patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Subcategory + merchantType assignment
            ├── CleanName.py            # Merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Statistical salary clustering
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer via fuzzy name match
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM rollup categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # Human-readable summary text
            ├── CardCleanNames.py / CardPurpose.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── Transaction*Enums.py    # Category/subcategory enums
```

**No test files exist** anywhere in the repo (`*test*`, `*spec*` empty).  
**Git history:** single commit `0a1b6a3 import codebase` — no incremental diffs for “recent changes.”

---

## How the labeling pipeline works

### API entry

`POST /categorizeTransaction` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`

Payload fields: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`.

### Per-bank pipeline (identical shape for every bank)

```
1. AppUtil.clean_input_df          # strip description, numeric amount/balance
2. categorize_{BANK}_transactions  # BankScripts/* — primary labeling
3. [CREDIT_CARD only]
     card_clean_names → card_purpose
4. purpose(transactions, accountType)     # UtilityScripts/Purpose.py
5. clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)  # UtilityScripts/CleanName.py
6. [if accountHolder]
     internal_payment(...)
7. [if accountType == "SAVING"]
     salary_detection(...)
8. [if isPFMEnabled]
     pfm_categorization → simple_description
```

**Important ordering:** bank scripts extract `partyName` first; `purpose()` runs **before** `clean_names()`, so most subcategory rules see bank-raw names, not merchant-normalized ones. `clean_names` can still overwrite some subcategories at the end.

### What each stage produces

| Field | Set by |
|--------|--------|
| `transactionCategory` | Bank script (`np.select` rules, default `"TRANSFER"`); sometimes overwritten in `purpose` |
| `transactionSubcategory` | Bank script (partial) → `purpose` (main) → `clean_names` (few) → `salary_detection` / `internal_payment` |
| `partyName` / `party2` | Bank script extraction → `clean_names` merchant map |
| `merchantType` | Bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names` |
| `isInternalPayment` | `internal_payment` |
| PFM fields | `pfm_categorization` / `simple_description` |

### Rule engine pattern (everywhere)

```python
conditions_choices = [
    [boolean_mask_Series, "LABEL_OR_EXTRACTED_VALUE"],
    ...
]
df = pd.DataFrame(conditions_choices, columns=['conditions', 'choices'])
col = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=...)
```

**First true condition wins.** Order is critical.

### Narration parsing helpers (`AppUtil.py`)

- `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` → `desc.split('/')[n1:n2].join('')` — one slash segment  
- `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_colon`, …  
- `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` — `str.extract` capture group  

Bank scripts use these heavily for UPI/IMPS/NEFT/`BIL/` layouts.

### Cross-bank subcategory rules (`Purpose.py` + `RegexConstants.py`)

Huge keyword lists (`SALARY`, `LOAN_REP`, `UTILITY`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, …). Match against `description`, `partyName`, and compacted `party2`. Also assigns `merchantType` (Electricity, NBFC, Flight, …).

### Merchant normalization (`CleanName.py`)

~1900 lines of known-merchant rewrites (DTH, electricity boards, apps, banks). Ends with limited subcategory overrides (e.g. Paytm Wallet → `TRANSFER_TO_WALLET`).

### Salary detection (`SalaryDetection.py`)

Clustering on `party2` (Levenshtein), mode amount/frequency heuristics. **Requires non-empty `partyName`** for the candidate set (`partyName.str.len().gt(0)`). Bare-numeric narrations with empty party never enter the detector.

---

## Key file paths (absolute) with roles

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Routes; wires bank → purpose → clean → salary → PFM |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` | HDFC category + party; **bugs 1 & 4 hotspots** |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` | ICICI; **bugs 2, 3, 4** |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/SBI.py` | SBI; **bug 2** (`TRF_STOP_WORDS`) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/{Axis,Kotak,YES,UCO,PNB,BOB,RBL,BankOfMaharashtra,Indusind,TamilnadMerchantile}.py` | Numeric-remark cheque rules (short lengths only) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | Slash/dash splitters, extract |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Shared purpose/salary/bounce regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank patterns; `TRF_STOP_WORDS`, `HDFC_CLEAN1`, cheque/FT patterns |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Cross-bank subcategory / merchantType |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Merchant name cleanup |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Statistical salary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self-pay fuzzy match |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | PFM rollups |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Category enum labels |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Subcategory enum labels |

**Tests:** none.

---

## Suspicious code mapped to the 4 bugs

### Bug 1 — Long all-numeric credit → generic `TRANSFER`; bare numeric salary loses `SALARY`

**Cheque-by-numeric-remark is length-capped or ultra-specific**

| Bank | Rule | What matches |
|------|------|----------------|
| Axis, PNB, Indusind, BOM | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` | 5–6 digits only |
| YES, UCO | `remark ^[0-9]{3,6}$` | 3–6 digits |
| Kotak, BOB | `remark ^[0-9]{3,5}$` | 3–5 digits |
| RBL | `remark ^[0-9]{1,3}$` | 1–3 digits |
| **HDFC** | `remark.len==15` AND `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` | only `00000000000` + 5 digits |

HDFC (`HDFC.py` ~100):

```python
[(transactions.remark.str.len().eq(15)) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT")
 & transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}", ...), "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"]
```

A **long all-numeric** reference (e.g. 10+ digits, not padded zeros) fails every bank’s cheque heuristic → default **`TRANSFER`**. That matches “used to show as cheque deposit, now reads as generic transfer” if remark formats lengthened or zero-padding changed.

**Bare-numeric salary — hard bugs**

HDFC subcategory (`HDFC.py` ~124):

```python
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER")
 & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", ...)
 & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT")
 & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],   # <-- SAVINGS
```

Controller always passes **`accountType == "SAVING"`** (no trailing S). This rule **never fires**.

Also:

- Only exact **6-digit** description.
- `Purpose.py` salary needs keyword match (`SALARY` / `"salary"` / `SAL_IMPS`) — bare digits miss.
- `SalaryDetection` drops empty `partyName` candidates — numeric-only credits with blank party never get statistical salary.

So bare numeric salary credits stay `TRANSFER` with empty subcategory unless some other path hits.

---

### Bug 2 — Narration opens with direction word → empty/wrong counterparty

**SBI — stop-word wipe**

`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:65`:

```python
TRF_STOP_WORDS = "...|Transfer To.*|Transfer From.*|...|^To Transfer.*|..."
```

Applied in `SBI.py` ~190:

```python
transactions['partyName'] = transactions['partyName'].replace(
    to_replace=TRF_STOP_WORDS, value="", regex=True)
```

If extracted party is `"Transfer To JOHN DOE"`, pattern `Transfer To.*` **erases the entire string** → empty counterparty.

Extraction (`SBI.py` ~131–132) only strips `TRANSFER TO/FROM` + **11-digit** account:

```python
.replace(to_replace="TRANSFER TO [0-9]{11}", value="", regex=True)
```

Name-only forms (`TRANSFER TO RAHUL`) keep the prefix, then get wiped by `TRF_STOP_WORDS`.

Also ~181 strips `[Tt]ransfer To|[Tt]ransfer From` but not bare `^To `|`^From ` on leftover names.

**ICICI — wrong capture group**

`ICICI.py` ~159:

```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("TRFR TO:|TRFR FROM:", ...)
 , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)]
```

`index=0` is **`TO`/`FROM`**, not the name (`index=1`). Party becomes `"To"` / `"From"`, then often blanked by `^[A-Z]$` cleanup (~235).

**HDFC — aggressive “transfer” clean**

`HDFC_CLEAN1` includes bare `transfer` (`BankRegexConstants.py` ~106). Any `partyName` containing “transfer” is blanked (`HDFC.py` ~252).

Direction handling exists only for some prefixes (`^Trn?f To |^Paid To |...` ~256–257); many variants (`FROM X`, `BY TRANSFER X`) incomplete.

**Karnataka** does the right thing for `^To ` (`KarurVyasa`/`Karnataka` style extract). Inconsistent across banks.

**UnionBank** strips `Transfer|^To` after title-case (~144) — better, but still bank-local.

---

### Bug 3 — Slash-delimited bill refs: numeric field taken as payee

**ICICI `BIL/` extraction** (`ICICI.py` ~147–151):

```python
# BIL/INFT/ with exactly 3 slashes → segment index 2
[^BIL/INFT/ & count("/").eq(3), sep_by_(..., 2, 3)]

# BIL/BPAY|BBPS|INFT|NEFT longer forms → index 4
[^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|...|^BIL/INFT|^BIL/NEFT, sep_by_(..., 4, 5)]

# BIL/BPAY|RCHG|ONL → index 3
[^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL, sep_by_(..., 3, 4)]

# BIL/001|002/... → index 2, then strip digits
[^BIL/00[12].*/.*/(?!(NSP)), sep_by_(..., 2, 3).replace(r'\d+', '')]
```

For layout `type / sub-type / numeric_ref / payee_name`:

| segments | indices | payee should be |
|----------|---------|-----------------|
| 4 parts | 0,1,2,3 | **3** |

Rules that take **index 2** pick the **numeric ref**.  
`sep_by_(d, n1, n2)` only returns **one** segment (`[n1:n2]`).

Later cleanup (`ICICI.py` ~233):

```python
[partyName contains [0-9]{6,} & not CMS/INTERNAL → ""]
```

Pure long numerics become empty; short/alphanumeric refs can **stick as the name** — “lifting numeric reference into name instead of final payee.”

Similar fixed-index slash picks appear in Axis/IDFC/UnionBank NEFT-IMPS paths; ICICI bill path is the clearest match to the reported shape.

Also note `np.select` **later rules override earlier ones** when multiple conditions are true — later broader `^BIL/INFT` / `^INF/` rules can stomp more specific earlier extractions depending on mask overlap.

---

### Bug 4 — Immediate offsetting credit labeled bounce, not reversal

**Only a few banks use adjacent-row heuristics:**

**HDFC.py ~98–99 — clear logic bug:**

```python
# Intended REVERSAL for channelled payments — but compares description to shift(2)
[CREDIT & prev DEBIT & same amount
 & description.eq(description.shift(periods=2))   # <-- should almost certainly be periods=1
 & description contains IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS
 → "REVERSAL"]

# Catch-all BOUNCE — same amount, same description as immediate previous debit
[CREDIT & prev DEBIT & same amount
 & description.eq(description.shift(periods=1))
 → "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE"]
```

Because `shift(2)` almost never equals the debit’s description, **REVERSAL rarely matches**. The next rule then marks **any** same-description, same-amount credit right after a debit as **`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`**, including failed/reversed transfers that should be REVERSAL.

**ICICI.py ~49–50:**

```python
# REVERSAL: same desc shift(1) + IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS  (correct shift)
# AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE: same desc shift(1), NO channel filter
```

Order is correct for channelled rails (REVERSAL first). Offsetting credits on **other** categories (FT, ACH, plain TRANSFER, bill pay, etc.) still become **BOUNCE**.

**Saraswat.py** only has the REVERSAL half (channelled).  
**StandardCharted** bounce only for `NACH DR IW`.  
**DCB** uses shift for NEFT return only.

No shared “reversal vs bounce” utility — each bank reimplements with subtle differences. HDFC’s `shift(periods=2)` is the strongest smoking gun.

Also: rules assume chronological order of the input DataFrame; unsorted statements break both paths.

---

## Additional boundary / consistency issues

1. **`SAVING` vs `SAVINGS`** — Controller/`Purpose`/`InternalPayment` use `SAVING`; HDFC salary rule uses `SAVINGS` → dead code.  
2. **Default category `TRANSFER`** — any unmatched narration falls here; numeric-only credits are especially vulnerable.  
3. **`purpose` clears subcategory** for categories matching `REFUND|…|BOUNCE|…` (`Purpose.py` ~173) — mis-tagged bounce loses useful sub-tags.  
4. **Cheque deposit vs salary** — bare numeric credit can’t be both; cheque rules often require short remark lengths; salary needs keywords or the broken HDFC 6-digit path.  
5. **No tests** — regressions on remark length, slash index, direction words, and shift windows have no safety net.  
6. **Single git snapshot** — cannot attribute “now vs used to” to a specific commit inside this repo; the broken boundaries above are present in the imported tree as-is.

---

## Suggested investigation priority (by bug)

| Bug | Primary files | Highest-confidence defect |
|-----|---------------|---------------------------|
| 1 Cheque/salary numeric | `HDFC.py`, cheque `remark` rules in Axis/Kotak/YES/…, `Purpose.py`, `SalaryDetection.py` | HDFC `SAVINGS` typo; remark length caps; salary needs keywords/party |
| 2 Direction prefix | `SBI.py` + `TRF_STOP_WORDS`, `ICICI.py:159`, `HDFC.py` + `HDFC_CLEAN1` | `Transfer To.*` full wipe; `py_extract` index 0 |
| 3 Bill slash payee | `ICICI.py` BIL/ block ~147–151, `AppUtil.sep_by_` | Fixed segment index 2/3/4 vs final name field |
| 4 Bounce vs reversal | `HDFC.py:98–99`, `ICICI.py:49–50` | HDFC `shift(2)`; bounce catch-all without channel/intent guards |

I can go deeper on any one bank’s full rule list or sketch concrete fix patches next if you want.
</task_result>
</task>

Looking at BOB more carefully - it has CHEQUE_DEPOSIT for remark but I only saw DEBIT for CHEQUE_PAID with remark. Let me check BOB again.
The maintainer note points to a subtle edge case in the ICICI bounce rule that’s catching a legitimate reversal instead of the intended bounce. The current logic is:

- REVERSAL matches any IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS first  
- bounce catch-all then matches everything else with same amount/desc after 1–2 rows

But when the reversal is non-channelled (or the channelled rule is broken), the reversal never fires and the bounce rule swallows it.

Proposed fix for ICICI bounce:

```python
# Only treat as bounce if the debit was AUTO_PAYMENT category
# (or contains bounce keywords)
BO = (
    CREDIT
    & prev.amount.eq(-amount)
    & prev.description.eq(description)
    & prev.category.isin({"AUTO_PAYMENT", "BILL_PAYMENT"})
    & ~prev.description.str.contains("REVERSAL|REVERSE", na=False)
)
```

This keeps the existing bounce behaviour for normal auto payments while letting non-channelled reversals (and the HDFC shift(2) case) fall through to REVERSAL.
